purpose: Test whether the directional scheduler result from one in-repository parser target generalizes to a second structurally different parser while keeping target execution, corpus evolution, mutation families, policy parameters, run count, and per-target execution budgets inspectable and reproducible.

campaign.reward: 1 iff the executed child input exposes at least one target trace feature not previously seen by that policy on that target in the run; otherwise 0

targets.traceModel: binary framed-record states covering magic bytes, version/flags, declared-length relations, payload tokens/braces, and checksum states
ASCII command-language states covering line structure, command recognition, key/value forms, authorization forms, separators, quoting, and batch subcommands

interpretationBoundary: Both targets are committed executable research harnesses, not external benchmark or production programs.
Target-specific dictionaries are allowed, while the four-dimensional LinUCB context definition and policy parameters are shared across targets.
Trace features are explicit parser branch/state markers, not compiler-instrumented AFL++ edge coverage.
The campaign does not use AFL++, libFuzzer, sanitizers, crash discovery, or fault triage.
Per-target feature counts are reported separately because the two trace spaces have different semantics and sizes; no pooled raw feature-count winner is manufactured.
The study is exploratory and preserves target-to-target directional disagreement without inferential significance claims.
